reading.title: Living Abroad
reading.text:
When Sophie moved from Bristol to Spain, she expected the first few months to be easy. She had visited the country several times on holiday and had always loved the weather and the food. However, living abroad turned out to be very different from visiting.
At first, she found everyday tasks difficult. Simple things, such as opening a bank account or going to the doctor, were stressful because of the language. She often felt lonely and missed her family.
Gradually, things improved. She joined a local Spanish class, where she met other newcomers, and slowly she began to make friends. After a year, she felt completely at home. 'Moving abroad was the hardest thing I have ever done,' she says, 'but also the best.'

quiz.e: She felt lonely and missed her family.

quiz.e: She met newcomers at a local Spanish class.

quiz.e: The hardest thing she'd done, but also the best.

reading.title: The Power of Habit
reading.text:
Most of us would like to change something about our lives — to exercise more, eat better, or waste less time. Yet good intentions are rarely enough. Research suggests that the secret to lasting change is not willpower, but habit.
A habit is an action we repeat so often that it becomes automatic. Once a behaviour becomes a habit, we no longer have to think about it or force ourselves to do it. The difficulty, of course, is building the habit in the first place.
Experts recommend starting small. Instead of promising to run for an hour every day, you might begin with just ten minutes. It is also helpful to attach a new habit to an existing one — for example, doing a few exercises straight after brushing your teeth. If you keep the goal small and repeat it daily, it will eventually feel natural.

quiz.q: According to the text, what is the secret to lasting change?
quiz.e: The text says habit, not willpower.

quiz.q: What is a habit?
quiz.e: A habit is a repeated, automatic action.

quiz.e: Once automatic, no effort is needed.

quiz.e: Attach the new habit to an existing one.

reading.title: A Letter of Complaint
reading.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a jacket I bought from your online shop on 3 May (order number 4471).

When the jacket arrived, I was very disappointed. Although the website described it as dark blue, the jacket I received was clearly black. Furthermore, there was a small hole in one of the pockets, which suggests it had not been checked properly before being sent.

I have been a regular customer for several years and have never had a problem before. However, on this occasion I am not satisfied with the quality of the product or the service.

I would therefore like a full refund. I have attached a photograph of the jacket as evidence. I look forward to hearing from you within seven days.

Yours faithfully,
J. Harris

quiz.e: It is a letter of complaint about a jacket.

quiz.e: It was black instead of dark blue.

quiz.q: What other fault did the jacket have?
quiz.e: There was a hole in one pocket.

reading.title: The Interview
reading.text:
Emily had prepared for weeks. She had researched the company, practised her answers, and chosen her clothes carefully the night before. By the time the morning arrived, she felt ready — or so she thought.
The trouble began on the way there. Her train was cancelled, and by the time she found another, she was already running late. When she finally reached the office in Manchester, she was twenty minutes behind and out of breath.
To her surprise, the manager was understanding. He explained that one of his own interviews, years earlier, had gone badly for similar reasons, and he had still been offered the job. The interview went well, and Emily relaxed.
A week later, an email arrived. She had got the job. Looking back, she realised that the disaster on the way had actually helped: it had shown the manager how she behaved under pressure.

quiz.q: How had Emily prepared for the interview?
o: She researched, practised and chose clothes.
quiz.e: She researched, practised answers and chose clothes.

quiz.e: He was understanding and shared his own story.

quiz.q: What was the result?
quiz.e: A week later she got the job.

quiz.q: Why does she think the difficult journey helped?
o: It showed how she behaves under pressure.
quiz.e: It showed the manager how she handled pressure.

grammar.title: Third conditional
grammar.lead: The third conditional talks about unreal situations in the past — things that did not happen — and their imagined results. We use it to express regret, criticism or relief about the past.

leadTr.uz: Uchinchi shart gapi o'tmishdagi bo'lmagan voqealar va ularning xayoliy natijalari haqida: afsus, tanqid va tahlil uchun ishlatiladi. If + past perfect, would have + V3.
leadTr.ru: Третий кондиционал — о несостоявшемся прошлом и его воображаемых результатах: сожаление, критика, анализ. If + past perfect, would have + V3.

grammar.situation: “If I had studied medicine, I would have become a doctor.” — But I didn’t study medicine, so I’m not a doctor. The third conditional imagines a different past.

blocks.h: Form: if + past perfect, would have + past participle
p: Both clauses refer to an imagined past that is now impossible to change.
ex: If I had studied, I would have passed.

p: Use could have (ability/possibility) or might have (possible result) instead of ‘would have’.
ex: If we’d left earlier, we could have caught the train. · She might have won if she’d tried.

p: ‘I’d’ can mean ‘I had’ or ‘I would’. In the if-clause it is ‘had’; in the result it is ‘would’.
ex: If I’d known (had), I’d have told you (would).

p: Express regret, criticism, or relief about a finished situation.
ex: If you’d listened, this wouldn’t have happened.

grammar.tip: Never use ‘would have’ in the if-clause: ‘If I would have known’ is wrong → ‘If I had known, I would have…’.
examples: "If I had known, I would have helped."
"She would have passed if she had revised."
"If we’d left earlier, we could have caught the bus."
"They might have won if they had played better."
"If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone out."
"You wouldn’t have got lost if you’d used a map."

mistakes.v: If I had known, I’d have called. (no “would” after if)

grammar.title: Mixed conditionals
grammar.lead: Mixed conditionals combine two time frames. The most common type links a past condition to a present result, or a present condition to a past result.

leadTr.uz: Aralash shart gaplari ikki vaqtni birlashtiradi: eng ko'p uchraydigani — o'tmishdagi shartning hozirgi natijasi: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
leadTr.ru: Смешанные кондиционалы соединяют два времени: чаще всего прошлое условие с настоящим результатом: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.

p: if + past perfect, would + base. A past action affects the present.
ex: If I had taken the job, I would be rich now.

p: if + past simple, would have + past participle. A present (general) fact affects the past.
ex: If I were more careful, I wouldn’t have made that mistake.

p: Words like now, today, still often signal a present result from a past cause.
ex: If she hadn’t missed the flight, she would be here now.

p: Mixed conditionals are unreal in both clauses; only the time frames differ.
ex: If I spoke French (now), I would have understood them (then).

grammar.tip: Decide the time of each clause separately: if the cause is past, use past perfect; if the result is present, use ‘would + base’ (not ‘would have’).
examples: "If I had saved money, I would be on holiday now."
"If she were taller, she would have joined the team."
"If we hadn’t moved, we would still live in Leeds."
"If he weren’t so shy, he would have spoken to her."
"If I had learnt to drive, life would be easier now."
"If you liked sport, you would have come with us."

mistakes.v: …I would be a doctor now. (present result → would + base)

If I book, we would be there now.
If I'd booked, we would have been there now.
If I booked, we will be there.

quiz.q: Complete: 'If she didn't hate flying, she ___ to Japan with us last year.'
quiz.e: Present fact → past result: would have gone.

grammar.title: Wish & if only
grammar.lead: We use ‘wish’ and ‘if only’ to talk about things we would like to be different. The tense we choose shows whether we mean the present, the past, or an annoying situation we want to change.

leadTr.uz: 'Wish' va 'if only' narsalar boshqacha bo'lishini istaganda ishlatiladi. Tanlangan zamon hozirgi, o'tmish yoki bezovta qiluvchi odat haqida ekanini ko'rsatadi.
leadTr.ru: Wish и if only выражают желание, чтобы всё было иначе. Выбранное время показывает: речь о настоящем, прошлом или раздражающей привычке.

p: For present situations we want to be different, use the past simple (or ‘were’).
ex: I wish I had more time. · I wish I were taller.

p: For regrets about the past, use the past perfect.
ex: I wish I had studied harder.

p: For another person’s annoying behaviour, or a change we want, use would.
ex: I wish you would stop shouting. · I wish it would stop raining.

p: if only works like ‘wish’ but is more emphatic.
ex: If only I hadn’t said that!

grammar.tip: Don’t use ‘wish + would’ about yourself. Say ‘I wish I could…’, not ‘I wish I would…’. Use ‘would’ for other people’s behaviour.
examples: "I wish I knew the answer."
"I wish I hadn’t eaten so much."
"I wish you would listen to me."
"If only I were on holiday now."
"She wishes she had taken the job."
"If only it would stop snowing!"

mistakes.x: I wish I would be on holiday now.
mistakes.v: I wish I were on holiday now. (don’t use wish + would about yourself)

mistakes.x: I wish I would have studied harder.
mistakes.v: I wish I had studied harder.

quiz.q: I wish I ___ taller.
I wish I ___ harder for the exam (it's finished).
I wish you ___ stop interrupting me!
I wish I ___ more money right now.
If only it ___ raining!
She wishes she ___ the truth earlier.
I wish I ___ speak Chinese.
I wish my neighbours ___ so much noise.
If only I ___ that email — it was a mistake.
Choose the present wish.
Find the mistake: 'I wish I would be on holiday now.'
quiz.e: Don't use ‘wish + would’ about yourself: I wish I were.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I wish I ___ the job, and I wish they ___ me another chance.'
quiz.e: Past regret ‘had taken’ + wanting future change ‘would give’.

quiz.q: Which expresses a past regret?
o: I wish I had met her.

quiz.q: Complete: 'If only he ___ listen — he never does!'
Choose the correct sentence.
o: I wish I would have studied.

grammar.title: The passive: advanced
grammar.lead: At B2 we use the passive across all tenses and in impersonal reporting structures, which are common in news and academic writing to report opinions without naming a source.

leadTr.uz: B2 darajasida passiv barcha zamonlarda hamda 'It is said that…' kabi shaxssiz konstruksiyalarda ishlatiladi — bu yangiliklar va akademik uslubda keng tarqalgan.
leadTr.ru: На B2 пассив используется во всех временах и в безличных оборотах вроде It is said that… — это типично для новостей и академического стиля.

grammar.situation: “The painting is thought to be a fake.” / “It is said that he is very rich.” — Impersonal passive structures report opinions without naming who says them.

p: Form the passive with the correct tense of be + past participle, including perfect and continuous forms.
ex: The road is being repaired. · The work had been finished. · It will have been done.

p: Use It + is/was + reporting verb + that… to report general opinions.
ex: It is said that he is very rich. · It was believed that the Earth was flat.

p: A second pattern: Subject + is/was + said/thought + to + infinitive.
ex: He is said to be rich. · She is thought to have left the country.

p: Use have/get + object + past participle when someone does a service for you (see causatives).
ex: I had my car repaired.

grammar.tip: In ‘He is said to have left’, use the perfect infinitive (to have + pp) when the action is earlier than the reporting.
examples: "The bridge is being rebuilt at the moment."
"The results had been announced before we arrived."
"It is believed that prices will rise."
"The painting is thought to be a fake."
"He is said to have made a fortune."
"The decision will have been made by Friday."

mistakes.x: It is said that he has leave.
mistakes.v: …he has left. (past participle)

mistakes.x: He is thought to have stole it.
mistakes.v: He is thought to have stolen it.

quiz.q: The road ___ at the moment.
quiz.e: Present continuous passive: is being repaired.

quiz.q: The letters ___ before noon yesterday.
quiz.e: Past perfect passive: had been delivered.

quiz.q: It ___ that he is very wealthy.
quiz.e: Impersonal report: It is said that.

quiz.q: The house ___ by next week.
The matter is still ___.
It is believed ___ the painting is genuine.
He is said ___ a genius.
The project ___ by the end of the month.
quiz.e: Future perfect passive: will have been finished.

quiz.q: She is thought ___ the country.
Rewrite impersonally: 'People say she is rich.'
o: She is said to be rich.
quiz.e: She is said to be rich.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'It is said that he has leave the company.'
Complete: 'The new policy ___ since January.'
quiz.e: Present perfect passive: has been implemented.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: He is thought to have stolen it.
He is thought to have stole it.
quiz.e: to have + past participle: to have stolen.

quiz.q: Complete (continuous past passive): 'The house ___ when we drove past.'
quiz.e: Past continuous passive: was being built.

quiz.q: Rewrite: 'They believe the company has lost money.'
o: The company is believed to have lost money.
The company is believed losing money.
The company believes to lose money.
It is believed the company to lose money.
quiz.e: is believed to have lost money.

grammar.title: Reported speech: reporting verbs
grammar.lead: Beyond ‘say’ and ‘tell’, English uses many reporting verbs that summarise the function of what was said — such as offer, promise, suggest, admit and refuse — each with its own grammar pattern.

leadTr.uz: 'Say' va 'tell'dan tashqari aytilgan gapning MAQSADINI ifodalovchi fe'llar bor: offer, promise, suggest, admit, refuse — har biri o'z grammatik qolipiga ega.
leadTr.ru: Кроме say и tell есть глаголы, передающие ЦЕЛЬ сказанного: offer, promise, suggest, admit, refuse — у каждого своя грамматическая модель.

p: offer, promise, agree, refuse, threaten, decide.
ex: He offered to help. · She refused to answer.

p: advise, ask, tell, warn, remind, encourage, invite.
ex: They advised me to wait. · He warned us not to go.

p: suggest, admit, deny, recommend, mention.
ex: She suggested leaving early. · He admitted breaking it.

p: apologise for, insist on, accuse sb of, congratulate sb on.
ex: He apologised for being late. · She insisted on paying.

grammar.tip: Match the verb to its pattern: ‘suggest’ takes -ing or ‘that…’, never ‘to’. ‘He suggested to go’ is wrong → ‘He suggested going’.
examples: "She offered to drive me home."
"They warned us not to swim there."
"He admitted stealing the money."
"I apologised for forgetting her birthday."
"The doctor advised him to rest."
"She insisted on seeing the manager."

mistakes.x: She suggested to meet at six.
mistakes.v: She suggested meeting at six. (suggest + -ing)
He apologised for being late.

quiz.q: He offered ___ me with my bags.
She suggested ___ a taxi.
They advised me ___ a doctor.
He admitted ___ the window.
She refused ___ the question.
He apologised ___ late.
They warned us ___ out late.
quiz.e: warn + object + not to: not to stay.

quiz.q: She insisted ___ for dinner.
He denied ___ anything wrong.
They invited us ___ the party.
Find the mistake: 'She suggested to meet at six.'
Report: "I'll definitely pay you back." → He ___.
quiz.e: promise + to: promised to pay back.

quiz.q: Report: "It was me. I took it." → She ___.
Report: "You should rest." (doctor → patient)
o: The doctor advised him to rest.
The doctor suggested him to rest.
quiz.e: advise + object + to: advised him to rest.

quiz.q: Report: "Well done on passing!" → They ___.

grammar.title: Past modals of deduction
grammar.lead: To make guesses about the past, we use a modal verb + have + past participle. These show how certain we are that something happened, based on present evidence.

leadTr.uz: O'tmish haqidagi taxminlar uchun modal + have + V3 ishlatiladi: must have left — aniq ketgan; can't have known — bilgan bo'lishi mumkin emas.
leadTr.ru: Для догадок о прошлом: модальный глагол + have + V3. Must have left — точно ушёл; can't have known — не мог знать.

p: Use must have + past participle when you are sure something happened.
ex: The ground is wet — it must have rained.

p: Use can’t/couldn’t have + pp when you are sure it did not happen.
ex: He can’t have finished already; it’s too soon.

p: Use these for things that possibly happened but you’re not sure.
ex: She might have missed the bus. · They could have got lost.

p: Use should have + pp for the right thing that didn’t happen (regret or criticism).
ex: You should have told me. · I shouldn’t have eaten so much.

grammar.tip: For deduction the opposite of ‘must have’ is ‘can’t have’, not ‘mustn’t have’. ‘Mustn’t have’ is not used for deduction in standard English.
examples: "The lights are off — they must have gone out."
"She can’t have seen us; she didn’t wave."
"He might have forgotten the meeting."
"You should have called a doctor."
"I shouldn’t have said that."
"They could have taken the wrong road."

mistakes.x: He mustn’t have heard the bell.
mistakes.v: He can’t have heard the bell. (negative deduction → can’t have)
You should have called me.

quiz.q: The grass is wet. It ___ last night.
quiz.e: Sure it happened → must have rained.

quiz.q: He ___ the news; he looks shocked.
She didn't wave, so she ___ us.
I'm not sure where he is. He ___ home.
You're hurt! You ___ me.
The cake is gone. Someone ___ it.
He failed? He ___ much.
They're late. They ___ stuck in traffic.
I feel ill. I ___ that fish.
Choose the 'impossible' deduction.
quiz.e: can't have = sure it didn't happen.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'He mustn't have heard the bell.'
Complete: 'The door's open — someone ___ in, or you ___ to lock it.'
o: must have broken / might have forgotten
quiz.e: must have broken in (sure) + might have forgotten (possible).

quiz.q: Which shows regret about the past?
Complete: 'She passed easily — the exam ___ very hard.'
quiz.e: Sure it wasn't hard → can't have been.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: should have + past participle: should have called.

grammar.title: Relative clauses: advanced
grammar.lead: At B2 we use more formal relative structures: prepositions before the relative pronoun, ‘whose’ for possession, and quantifiers like ‘some of whom’ and ‘both of which’ in non-defining clauses.

leadTr.uz: B2 da rasmiyroq nisbiy tuzilmalar o'rganiladi: predlog + relative pronoun (in which), egalik uchun 'whose' hamda 'some of whom', 'both of which' kabi birikmalar.
leadTr.ru: На B2 — более формальные относительные конструкции: предлог + местоимение (in which), whose для принадлежности, some of whom, both of which.

p: In formal English the preposition can go before the relative pronoun (which/whom).
ex: The man to whom I spoke… · The house in which they live…

p: In everyday English we usually move the preposition to the end and may drop the pronoun.
ex: The man (who) I spoke to… · The house (that) they live in…

p: In non-defining clauses use all/some/many/none/both + of whom/which.
ex: I have three sisters, all of whom are doctors.

p: whose shows possession for people and things.
ex: A company whose products are famous… · The author, whose books I love…

grammar.tip: After a preposition use whom (not ‘who’) and which (not ‘that’): ‘the person to whom…’, ‘the tool with which…’. ‘To that’ and ‘to who’ are wrong here.
examples: "The colleague with whom I work is brilliant."
"This is the book about which we spoke."
"She has many friends, most of whom live abroad."
"They sell phones, none of which are cheap."
"He’s an artist whose work sells worldwide."
"The reason for which he left is unclear."

mistakes.x: The client to that I wrote replied.
mistakes.v: …to whom I wrote… (preposition + whom)

mistakes.x: I have two cousins, both of who are nurses.
mistakes.v: …both of whom are nurses.

quiz.q: The person ___ I spoke was helpful. (formal)
That's the house ___ which they were born.
quiz.e: born in a house → in which.

quiz.q: He's a writer ___ novels are famous.
Informal: 'The man I spoke ___.'
quiz.e: speak to → preposition at the end: to.

quiz.q: I have two cousins, both ___ whom are nurses.
The tool ___ which we cut it was sharp.
She has many fans, some ___ whom waited all night.
The company ___ products we use is British.
This is the issue ___ which we must decide.
Choose the formal version of 'the man I work with'.
o: the man with who I work
the man with whom I work
the man with that I work

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'The client to that I wrote replied.'
Complete: 'He owns three shops, ___ are in London.'
Which is correct and formal?
o: The report on which it is based is here.
The report on that it is based is here.
The report which it is based on which…
The report based which on it…

quiz.q: Complete: 'She interviewed ten people, ___ had experience.'
Choose the correct 'whose' sentence.
o: The painter who paintings sell well is here.
The painter whose paintings sell well is here.
The painter which paintings sell well is here.
The painter whom paintings sell well is here.

grammar.title: Causative: have/get something done
grammar.lead: We use the causative when we arrange for someone else to do a service for us, rather than doing it ourselves. The structure focuses on the result, not on who does the work.

leadTr.uz: Kauzativ (have/get something done) xizmatni o'zimiz emas, boshqa birov bajarishini bildiradi: I had my phone repaired — telefonimni tuzattirdim.
leadTr.ru: Каузатив (have/get something done) означает, что услугу выполняет кто-то другой: I had my phone repaired — мне починили телефон.

grammar.situation: “I don’t cut my own hair — I have it cut.” — The causative shows that someone does a service for you. The focus is on the result, not who does the work.

p: The standard structure: have + thing + past participle.
ex: I had my hair cut. · We had the house painted.

p: get is a more informal alternative to ‘have’.
ex: I got my car repaired. · She got her photo taken.

p: Change the tense of ‘have/get’ as needed.
ex: I’m having my eyes tested tomorrow. · He’s had his phone fixed.

p: The same structure can describe something bad that happened to you.
ex: She had her bag stolen. · They had their flight cancelled.

grammar.tip: The order is have + OBJECT + past participle, not ‘have + past participle + object’. Say ‘I had my car washed’, not ‘I had washed my car’ (that means you did it yourself).
examples: "I had my suit cleaned for the wedding."
"We’re getting the kitchen redecorated."
"He had his tooth taken out."
"She got her hair coloured."
"They had their car broken into."
"I need to have my passport renewed."

mistakes.x: I had repaired my bike at the shop.
mistakes.v: I had my bike repaired. (have + object + past participle)
I’ll have the roof fixed.

quiz.q: I ___ my hair cut yesterday.
quiz.e: Causative past: had my hair cut.

quiz.q: We're going to ___ the house painted.
She ___ her car repaired last week.
Choose the correct order.
He needs to have his eyes ___.
I'm ___ my photo taken tomorrow.
They ___ their windows cleaned every month.
She ___ her bag stolen on the train. (bad event)
We've just ___ the carpet cleaned.
quiz.e: Present perfect: have had → 'have just had'... here 'had' completes 'have just had'.

quiz.q: Choose the causative meaning 'someone did it for me'.
Find the mistake: 'I had repaired my bike at the shop.'
o: had repaired → had my bike repaired
quiz.e: Causative needs object + pp: had my bike repaired.

quiz.q: Complete: 'You should ___ that tooth ___.'
quiz.e: get + object + past participle: get it looked at.

quiz.q: Which describes an unpleasant event?
quiz.e: had his car stolen = bad event.

quiz.q: Complete: 'They ___ their flight ___ because of the storm.'
quiz.e: had + object + past participle: had it cancelled.

quiz.q: Choose the correct future causative.
o: I'll have fixed the roof for me.
quiz.e: have + object + past participle: have the roof fixed.

grammar.title: Gerunds & infinitives: advanced
grammar.lead: Some verbs are followed by either a gerund or an infinitive, but with a clear change of meaning. Knowing the difference lets you say exactly what you mean.

leadTr.uz: Ayrim fe'llardan keyin gerund ham, infinitiv ham keladi, lekin ma'no aniq o'zgaradi: remember doing (eslash) / remember to do (unutmaslik).
leadTr.ru: После некоторых глаголов возможны обе формы, но смысл меняется: remember doing (помнить, как делал) / remember to do (не забыть сделать).

p: + to = the duty comes after; + -ing = the memory comes before.
ex: Remember to lock the door. (do it) · I remember locking it. (memory)

p: stop + -ing = end the activity; stop + to = pause in order to do something.
ex: He stopped smoking. (quit) · He stopped to smoke. (paused)

p: try + -ing = experiment; try + to = attempt something difficult.
ex: Try adding salt. (experiment) · I tried to open it. (attempt)

p: regret + -ing = be sorry about the past; regret + to = be sorry to announce. mean + -ing = involve; mean + to = intend.
ex: I regret saying it. · I regret to inform you… · This job means travelling. · I meant to call.

grammar.tip: With ‘remember/forget’: use the infinitive for a task you must do, and the -ing form for a memory of something already done.
examples: "Please remember to post the letter."
"I’ll never forget meeting her."
"He stopped to rest for a minute."
"Try turning it off and on again."
"I regret to tell you the news is bad."
"Studying abroad means leaving home."

mistakes.x: I regret to tell him the truth; now he’s angry.
mistakes.v: I regret telling him… (regret + -ing = sorry about the past)

mistakes.x: On the walk we stopped taking photos. (meaning: paused to take)
mistakes.v: …we stopped to take photos. (pause in order to)

quiz.q: Remember ___ the door when you leave.
I remember ___ him at the party last year.
He stopped ___ because his lungs hurt. (quit)
On the walk, we stopped ___ photos.
quiz.e: Paused in order to → to take.

quiz.q: I regret ___ that I can't help.
quiz.e: Sorry to announce → regret to say.

quiz.q: The recipe didn't work. Try ___ more sugar.
I tried ___ the window, but it was stuck.
quiz.e: Attempt at something hard → tried to open.

quiz.q: This new job means ___ to another city.
I'm sorry, I meant ___ you earlier.
Don't forget ___ your medicine tonight.
Find the mistake: 'I regret to tell him the truth; now he's angry.'
quiz.e: Sorry about the past → regret telling.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I'll never forget ___ the Pyramids, but please remember ___ the tickets.'
Which means 'he paused his walk to make a call'?
quiz.e: stop + to = pause in order to.

quiz.q: Complete: 'We regret ___ you that the flight ___, so we tried ___ another route.'
o: to inform / has been cancelled / to find
quiz.e: regret to inform + passive + tried to find.

quiz.q: Choose the correct pair.
o: Remember posting it (do it now) / I stopped to smoke (quit).
Remember to post it (do it) / I stopped smoking (quit).
Remember to post it / I stopped to smoke means I quit.
Remember posting it means do it now.

grammar.title: Future perfect & continuous
grammar.lead: To talk about the future in detail, we use the future continuous for actions in progress at a future time, and the future perfect for actions that will be completed before a future point.

leadTr.uz: Kelajakni batafsil ifodalash uchun: future continuous — kelajakdagi paytda davom etadigan harakat; future perfect — muayyan muddatgacha tugaydigan harakat.
leadTr.ru: Для детального будущего: future continuous — действие в процессе в будущий момент; future perfect — действие, завершённое к сроку.

p: An action that will be in progress at a specific future time.
ex: This time tomorrow I will be flying to Rome.

blocks.h: Future perfect: will have + past participle
p: An action that will be finished before a future time, often with ‘by’.
ex: By 2030 they will have built the bridge.

p: Use by + time or by the time + clause with the future perfect.
ex: By the time you arrive, I will have left.

p: will have been + -ing stresses the duration up to a future point.
ex: By June I will have been working here for ten years.

grammar.tip: Use the future continuous for something happening at a future moment, and the future perfect for something completed before that moment.
examples: "At 8 pm I ’ll be having dinner."
"By Friday we ’ll have finished the report."
"This time next week she ’ll be lying on a beach."
"By the time he’s 30, he ’ll have travelled the world."
"In May I ’ll have been studying here for three years."
"Don’t call at six — I’ll be driving."

mistakes.x: By next month I will finish the course.
mistakes.v: By next month I will have finished… (completed before → future perfect)

mistakes.x: Don’t call at six — I will drive.
mistakes.v: …I’ll be driving. (in progress → future continuous)

quiz.q: This time tomorrow I ___ to Spain.
quiz.e: In progress at a future time → will be flying.

quiz.q: By next year, they ___ the new road.
quiz.e: Completed before a future time → will have built.

quiz.q: At 9 pm tonight, we ___ the match.
By the time you arrive, I ___.
Don't phone at six; I ___.
By Friday she ___ the project.
quiz.e: Completed by a deadline → will have finished.

quiz.q: This time next week, they ___ on holiday.
In June I ___ here for five years.
quiz.e: Duration up to a future point → will have been working.

quiz.q: By 2040, scientists ___ a cure, perhaps.
Choose the action in progress at a future time.
Find the mistake: 'By next month I will finish the course.'
quiz.e: Completed before a future time → will have finished.

quiz.q: Complete: 'At noon we ___ the test; by 2 pm we ___ it.'
o: will be taking / will have finished
will have taken / will be finishing
quiz.e: In progress ‘will be taking’ + completed ‘will have finished’.

quiz.q: Which stresses duration up to a future point?
o: By May I'll have been writing for a year.

quiz.q: Complete: 'By the time the film ends, we ___ here for three hours.'
quiz.e: Duration up to a point → will have been sitting.

quiz.q: Choose the correct future perfect.
quiz.e: will have + past participle: will have left.

grammar.title: Past perfect continuous
grammar.lead: The past perfect continuous shows that an activity had been in progress for a period before another point in the past. It emphasises duration and often explains a past situation.

leadTr.uz: Past perfect continuous o'tmishdagi nuqtadan OLDIN ma'lum muddat davom etgan faoliyatni bildiradi va ko'pincha sababni tushuntiradi: He was tired because he had been working.
leadTr.ru: Past perfect continuous — действие, длившееся ДО момента в прошлом; часто объясняет причину: He was tired because he had been working.

grammar.situation: “She had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally came.” — The past perfect continuous shows how long an activity had gone on up to a past moment.

p: Use had been + verb-ing for an action that continued up to a point in the past.
ex: She had been waiting for an hour when the bus came.

p: It often explains why something was the case at a past moment.
ex: His eyes were red because he had been crying.

p: Use for + period and since + starting point.
ex: They had been living there for years before they moved.

p: The continuous stresses the activity/duration; the simple stresses the completed result.
ex: I had been reading. (activity) · I had read the book. (finished)

grammar.tip: Don’t use the continuous with state verbs. Say ‘I had known her for years’, not ‘I had been knowing’.
examples: "He was tired because he had been working all night."
"We had been driving for hours when the car broke down."
"She had been studying French before she moved to Paris."
"The ground was wet; it had been raining."
"They had been arguing before we arrived."
"I had been waiting for ages when she finally called."

mistakes.x: I had been knowing him for years before he left.
mistakes.v: I had known him for years… (state verb → simple)

mistakes.x: They had been lived there for years.
mistakes.v: They had been living there for years.

quiz.q: She ___ for an hour when the bus arrived.
quiz.e: Duration up to a past point → had been waiting.

quiz.q: His eyes were red because he ___.
quiz.e: Explains the past result → had been crying.

quiz.q: They ___ for hours before they stopped.
The form of the past perfect continuous is ___.
It was wet outside; it ___.
We ___ for the train when it was cancelled.
quiz.e: Duration before a past event → had been waiting.

quiz.q: She was out of breath because she ___.
quiz.e: Explains the state → had been running.

quiz.q: How long ___ they ___ before they got married?
Which verb is WRONG in this form?
Choose the duration form.
o: I had been reading for hours.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I had been knowing him for years before he left.'
Complete: 'By the time help arrived, they ___ for three hours.'
quiz.e: Duration up to a past point → had been swimming.

quiz.q: Which stresses the completed result?
o: She had been painting the room.
She had been paint the room.
quiz.e: Completed → past perfect simple: had painted.

quiz.q: Complete: 'He failed because he ___ instead of revising.'
quiz.e: Ongoing activity explaining the result → had been playing.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: They had been lived there for years.
They had been living there for years.
They have been living there for years before.
They had living there for years.

grammar.title: Inversion
grammar.lead: In formal or emphatic English, certain negative or limiting adverbials at the start of a sentence force inversion — the auxiliary verb comes before the subject, as in a question.

leadTr.uz: Rasmiy va ta'sirli uslubda gap boshidagi inkor iboralar (never, rarely, not only) inversiyani talab qiladi — yordamchi fe'l egadan oldin keladi: Never have I seen…
leadTr.ru: В формальном стиле отрицательные обороты в начале предложения (never, rarely, not only) требуют инверсии: Never have I seen…

grammar.situation: “Never have I seen such a mess.” — In formal or emphatic English, a negative word at the start pushes the auxiliary in front of the subject, like a question.

p: After never, rarely, seldom, hardly, no sooner, not only, little at the start, invert subject and auxiliary.
ex: Never have I seen such a mess. · Rarely does she complain.

p: Used for one event quickly following another.
ex: Hardly had we arrived when it started to rain. · No sooner had he spoken than she left.

p: Not only + auxiliary + subject, … but also …
ex: Not only did he apologise, but he also paid.

p: After only then / only after / only when / not until, invert.
ex: Only when she left did I realise. · Not until midnight did they finish.

grammar.tip: Inversion uses the same auxiliary you’d use in a question: ‘Never have I…’, ‘Rarely does he…’, ‘Not only did she…’. Don’t use normal word order after these openers.
examples: "Never have I been so embarrassed."
"Rarely do we see such talent."
"Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang."
"No sooner had they left than it snowed."
"Not only is she clever, but she’s kind too."
"Only after the test did he relax."

mistakes.x: Never I have eaten such good food.
mistakes.v: Never have I eaten such good food. (invert: aux + subject)

mistakes.x: Not only she sings, but she dances.
mistakes.v: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

mistakes.x: No sooner he had left when it rained.
mistakes.v: No sooner had he left than it rained.

quiz.q: Never ___ such a beautiful view.
Rarely ___ to the cinema.
Not only ___ late, but he was rude too.
Seldom ___ such kindness.
Hardly ___ down when the bell rang.
No sooner had we left ___ it started to rain.
Little ___ that he was being watched.
Only when she apologised ___ better.
Not until the next day ___ the news.
Hardly had I arrived ___ the trouble began.
Find the mistake: 'Never I have eaten such good food.'
Complete: 'No sooner ___ the door ___ the alarm rang.'
quiz.e: No sooner had he opened … than.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: Not only she sings, but she dances.
Not only does she sing, but she also dances.
Not only sings she, but she dances.
Not only she does sing, but dances.
quiz.e: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

quiz.q: Complete: 'Only after he left ___ how rude he had been.'
quiz.e: Inversion after ‘Only after’: did I realise.

quiz.q: Rewrite with inversion: 'I had rarely felt so happy.'
o: Rarely I had felt so happy.
Rarely had I felt so happy.
Rarely did I had felt so happy.
quiz.e: Rarely had I felt so happy.

grammar.title: Cleft sentences
grammar.lead: Cleft (‘divided’) sentences split one idea into two clauses to emphasise a particular part. They are very common in speech for adding focus and contrast.

leadTr.uz: Cleft gaplar bitta fikrni ikki qismga bo'lib, kerakli joyga urg'u beradi: It was Aziz who called. / What I need is time. Og'zaki nutqda juda ko'p uchraydi.
leadTr.ru: Расщеплённые предложения делят мысль надвое ради акцента: It was Aziz who called. / What I need is time. Очень частотны в речи.

p: Emphasise a person, thing, time or place.
ex: It was Tom who broke it. · It was in 2010 that we met.

p: Emphasise the whole idea, often an action or need.
ex: What I need is a holiday. · What he did was (to) call the police.

blocks.h: The thing / the reason / the place
p: Other openers add focus too.
ex: The reason (why) I’m late is the traffic. · The place where we stayed was lovely.

p: All can mean ‘the only thing’.
ex: All I want is peace and quiet.

grammar.tip: In a What-cleft, the verb ‘be’ is singular even before a plural idea if ‘what’ is the subject: ‘What I need is answers’ (not ‘are’).
examples: "It was my sister who called, not me."
"It’s your help that I need."
"What surprised me was his honesty."
"What we did was book another flight."
"The reason I left was the noise."
"All she wanted was the truth."

mistakes.v: What I want is answers. (“what” as subject → singular verb)

mistakes.x: It was John which sent the email.
mistakes.v: It was John who sent the email.

quiz.q: ___ Tom who broke the window.
What I need ___ a long rest.
It was in Paris ___ they got married.
___ I want is some peace.
It was Sarah ___ helped me.
What he did ___ apologise.
The reason ___ I called was to thank you.
It's not the money ___ matters.
What surprised everyone ___ his decision.
Choose the cleft emphasising the place.
o: We stayed in a lovely hotel.
It was the hotel that we loved.
The place where we stayed was lovely.
quiz.e: The place where… = focus on place.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'What I want are answers.'
Rewrite to emphasise 'John': 'John sent the email.'
o: It was John who sent the email.
It was the email who John sent.
John it was sent the email.
quiz.e: It was John who sent the email.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ we should do ___ tell the truth.'
quiz.e: What we should do is tell the truth.

quiz.q: Which correctly emphasises the reason?
o: The reason why he left was the noise.
The reason what he left was the noise.
It was the reason the noise left.
Why the reason he left noise.
quiz.e: The reason why he left was the noise.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ that I admire ___ her honesty.'
quiz.e: The thing that I admire is her honesty.

grammar.title: Linking & contrast
grammar.lead: Linkers of contrast and concession join ideas that seem to conflict. The right choice depends on whether the linker is followed by a noun, an -ing form, or a full clause.

leadTr.uz: Qarama-qarshilik bog'lovchilari zid fikrlarni birlashtiradi. To'g'ri tanlov bog'lovchidan keyin ot, -ing shakli yoki to'liq gap kelishiga bog'liq: despite + ot, although + gap.
leadTr.ru: Союзы контраста и уступки соединяют противоречащие идеи. Выбор зависит от того, что идёт после: despite + сущ., although + предложение.

p: Followed by a subject + verb.
ex: Although it was late, we kept working. · Even though she tried, she failed.

p: Followed by a noun or -ing form, not a clause. Add ‘the fact that’ to use a clause.
ex: Despite the rain, we went out. · In spite of being tired, he worked. · Despite the fact that it rained…

p: Link two sentences; usually start a new sentence with a comma after.
ex: It was expensive. However, we bought it.

p: Show a direct contrast between two ideas.
ex: He likes tea, whereas she prefers coffee.

grammar.tip: Use ‘although’ before a clause and ‘despite / in spite of’ before a noun or -ing. ‘Despite it was raining’ is wrong → ‘Despite the rain’ or ‘Although it was raining’.
examples: "Although he was rich, he wasn’t happy."
"Despite the traffic, we arrived on time."
"In spite of feeling ill, she came."
"The plan was risky. Nevertheless, it worked."
"I love cities, whereas my brother prefers the countryside."
"Even though it costs more, it’s worth it."

mistakes.x: Despite it was cold, we swam.
mistakes.v: Although it was cold… / Despite the cold… (despite + noun, not a clause)

mistakes.x: Although it was hard but he tried.
mistakes.v: Although it was hard, he tried. (no “but” with although)

quiz.q: ___ it was raining, we went out.
___ the rain, we went out.
He likes coffee, ___ she prefers tea.
It was expensive. ___, we bought it.
In spite ___ the cost, they travelled.
___ being tired, she finished the race.
___ he studied hard, he didn't pass.
Choose the linker + clause.
The food was cold. ___, it tasted fine.
Despite ___ that it was late, they continued.
Find the mistake: 'Despite it was cold, we swam.'
quiz.e: Despite + noun/-ing; before a clause use ‘Although’.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ his wealth, he was unhappy, ___ his brother, who had little, was content.'
Which is correct?
o: In spite the danger, they climbed.
In spite of the danger, they climbed.
In spite of they were in danger, they climbed.
In spite that the danger, they climbed.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ being cheaper, the second option is better, ___ the first looks nicer.'
Choose the sentence that links two contrasting sentences.
o: Although it was hard, however we tried.
It was hard. However, we tried.
However it was hard we tried.

grammar.title: Articles & determiners: advanced
grammar.lead: At B2, article choice depends on shades of meaning: specific vs. general, the use of ‘the’ with unique reference, and fixed patterns with quantifiers and abstract nouns.

leadTr.uz: B2 da artikl tanlash ma'no nozikliklariga bog'liq: aniq va umumiy ma'no, yagona narsalar bilan 'the' hamda mavhum otlar bilan turg'un qoliplar.
leadTr.ru: На B2 выбор артикля зависит от оттенков: конкретное против общего, the с уникальными объектами, устойчивые модели с абстрактными существительными.

p: Use the when context makes the noun specific, after superlatives, and with ‘the only/same/first’.
ex: The book you lent me was great. · He’s the best. · It’s the only way.

p: Use no article for plural and uncountable nouns talking in general.
ex: Happiness matters. · Children learn fast. · I study history.

p: the + adjective can mean a whole group of people.
ex: The rich get richer. · The government helps the unemployed.

p: Use of with the/my/these: ‘most of the students’, ‘none of my friends’; without ‘of’ for general: ‘most students’.
ex: Most of the water was gone. · Most water is recycled here.

grammar.tip: Use ‘the’ when the noun is made specific by context (‘the book you lent me’), but no article for general statements with plurals/uncountables (‘books are useful’).
examples: "The information you gave me was helpful."
"Knowledge is power."
"She wants to help the poor."
"Most of the guests had left."
"He’s the first to arrive."
"I don’t drink coffee."

mistakes.v: …in nature. (general uncountable → no article)

mistakes.x: He gave me an useful advice.
mistakes.v: He gave me useful advice. (advice is uncountable)

quiz.q: ___ book you recommended was excellent.
quiz.e: Specified by context → The book you recommended.

quiz.q: ___ is important for everyone. (general)
The government should help ___.
quiz.e: the + adjective = the group: the poor.

quiz.q: ___ of the students passed.
She's ___ only person who knows.
I love ___ in general. (plural, general)
___ water in this bottle is dirty.
___ students learn at different speeds. (general)
He was ___ first to finish.
Choose the general statement.
Find the mistake: 'I'm interested in the nature.'
Complete: '___ rich should pay more tax, and ___ advice you gave was wise.'
Which is correct?
o: Most of the people hard work.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She studies ___ history of ___ art.'
quiz.e: ‘the history of art’: specified ‘the history’, general ‘art’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He gave me an useful advice.
He gave me a useful advice.
He gave me the useful advices.
quiz.e: ‘advice’ is uncountable → no article, no plural.

grammar.title: Subject–verb agreement in long sentences
grammar.lead: When the subject and the verb are separated by long phrases, it becomes easy to match the verb to the wrong noun. Train yourself to find the true subject first — then choose the verb form.

leadTr.uz: Ega va kesim orasida uzun iboralar bo'lsa, fe'lni noto'g'ri otga moslashtirish oson. Avval haqiqiy egani toping — keyin fe'l shaklini tanlang.
leadTr.ru: Когда подлежащее и сказуемое разделены длинными оборотами, легко согласовать глагол не с тем словом. Сначала найдите настоящее подлежащее — затем выбирайте форму глагола.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The collection of handwritten letters from the early twentieth century [___] recently been donated to the university library.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Cross out 'of handwritten letters from the early twentieth century.' Subject = 'collection' (singular) → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee on environmental standards [___] voted to adopt stricter regulations on industrial emissions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Committee' is a collective noun — singular in American English. It acts as a unit → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'A number of studies examining the long-term effects of sleep deprivation on cognitive function [___] produced alarming results.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'A number of X' = PLURAL → have. (Contrast: 'The number of studies HAS grown' — 'the number' = singular.)

quiz.q:
Text: 'The team of researchers, along with several graduate students, [___] presented findings at last month's conference.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Along with several graduate students' is an intervening phrase — cross it out. Subject = 'The team' (singular collective noun) → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The number of species affected by climate change [___] grown dramatically since the 1980s.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The number of X' = SINGULAR → has. Cross out 'of species affected by climate change.' Subject = 'the number' → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Every student, teacher, and administrator in the district [___] required to complete the new training module.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: When 'every' or 'each' precedes a compound subject joined by 'and,' the subject is still treated as SINGULAR. 'Every student, teacher, and administrator' → singular → is.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The report, together with its supporting appendices, [___] submitted to the board last Friday.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Together with its supporting appendices' is an intervening phrase (cross it out). Subject = 'The report' (singular) → was.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The policy changes announced by the administration [___] sparked widespread debate among educators.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Cross out the intervening phrase 'announced by the administration.' Subject = 'changes' (plural) → have.

quiz.q:
Text: 'There [___] a series of unresolved questions about the long-term safety of the compound.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Inverted sentence — find the subject after 'There ___.' Subject = 'a series' (singular collective noun) → is. 'A series of X' = singular.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The jury [___] still deliberating when the judge called for a recess.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Jury' = collective noun, singular in American English → was. The jury acts as a unified body.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Neither the proposed budget nor the alternative plans [___] received sufficient support from the full council.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Neither...nor': verb agrees with the CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'plans' (plural) → have.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Each of the participating countries [___] agreed to reduce carbon emissions by at least 30 percent by 2030.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Each' is always SINGULAR regardless of the following noun. Cross out 'of the participating countries.' Subject = 'each' → has.

grammar.title: Pronouns: agreement & clear reference
grammar.lead: A pronoun must match its noun in number and refer to it unambiguously. These exercises train both: choosing the right pronoun and keeping the reference clear.

leadTr.uz: Olmosh o'z oti bilan son jihatdan mos kelishi va unga aniq ishora qilishi kerak. Bu mashqlar ikkalasini ham rivojlantiradi: to'g'ri olmoshni tanlash va ishorani aniq saqlash.
leadTr.ru: Местоимение должно совпадать с существительным в числе и однозначно на него указывать. Эти упражнения тренируют и выбор местоимения, и ясность ссылки.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The government announced [___] intention to reform the tax code before the end of the fiscal year.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The government' is a singular collective noun → 'its.' A (their) treats it as plural.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Each candidate must prepare [___] own statement of purpose before the interview.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Each' = singular. In formal written English, 'each candidate' takes 'his or her.' C is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The research team, frustrated by the lack of funding, decided to publish [___] preliminary findings independently.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Research team' is a collective noun acting as a unit → singular → 'its.' But as members sharing intellectual agency, 'their' is also increasingly accepted. In this context — 'publish findings' as a unified act — B (its) is more formally precise.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The corporation restructured [___] operations to reduce overhead costs in the wake of declining revenues.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The corporation' = singular → 'its.' A (their) incorrectly treats it as plural.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The company and [___] subsidiary both reported strong earnings for the third quarter.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The company' is singular. 'Its subsidiary' — the subsidiary belongs to the singular company → 'its.' A is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'No one should be forced to compromise [___] principles simply to advance a career.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'No one' = SINGULAR indefinite pronoun → 'his or her' in formal register. C is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee published [___] annual report outlining the progress made toward achieving sustainability goals.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The committee' = singular collective noun → 'its.' D is correct. A (their) is incorrect for a singular noun. B (it's) = 'it is' — wrong word.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Both the director and the lead actor acknowledged [___] debt to the playwright's original vision.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Both X and Y' = plural → 'their.' C is correct. They share a collective debt.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The university updated [___] admissions policy to consider a wider range of socioeconomic factors.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The university' = singular → 'its.' C is correct. A (their) is plural. B (it's) = 'it is.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'Each country in the alliance pledged to increase [___] defense budget by two percent over the next decade.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Each country' — 'each' modifies 'country' (singular) → 'its.' B is correct. Though 'their' is increasingly used informally, 'its' is more formally precise for a singular noun.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Neither of the lead researchers was willing to retract [___] published findings without further evidence.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Neither of the lead researchers' — 'neither' is singular → 'his or her.' B is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The board of directors voted to approve the merger despite [___] concerns about the valuation.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The board of directors' = singular collective noun → 'its.' A is correct. The board as a unified body has 'its' concerns.

grammar.title: Commas & semicolons
grammar.lead: The comma and the semicolon are where most writing mistakes live. Learn when two ideas need a semicolon, when a comma is enough, and when neither belongs.

leadTr.uz: Vergul va nuqtali vergul — yozuvdagi xatolarning ko'pchiligi shu yerda. Ikki fikr qachon nuqtali vergul talab qilishini, qachon vergul yetarli ekanini o'rganing.
leadTr.ru: Запятая и точка с запятой — где живёт большинство ошибок письма. Учитесь понимать, когда двум идеям нужна точка с запятой, когда достаточно запятой, а когда не нужно ничего.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The experiment produced unexpected results[___] the team immediately redesigned the protocol.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The bridge, which was built in 1923[___] has withstood numerous earthquakes without significant structural damage.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Which was built in 1923' is a NONRESTRICTIVE clause — it adds information but doesn't identify which bridge. Nonrestrictive elements need commas on BOTH sides. The opening comma is present; a closing comma is needed here. A (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'After carefully analyzing three years of climate data[___] the researchers concluded that temperatures had risen faster than projected.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: An introductory participial phrase ('After carefully analyzing...') must be followed by a comma before the main clause. C (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The students who complete all required coursework[___] will be eligible to graduate in May.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Who complete all required coursework' is RESTRICTIVE — it identifies WHICH students (not all students, only those who complete coursework). No commas around restrictive clauses. B (no punctuation) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The novel, written over a period of ten years[___] draws on the author's experiences living in three different countries.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Written over a period of ten years' is a nonrestrictive participial phrase providing extra information about the novel. It needs commas on BOTH sides. The opening comma is already there; a closing comma is needed. B (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Scientists have long studied the effects of sleep deprivation[___] researchers continue to discover new neurological consequences.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two independent clauses. A comma alone = comma splice (A wrong). C (semicolon) correctly joins two independent clauses. B adds 'and' with a comma — also grammatically correct, but since we're choosing from four options, C (semicolon) is the clean correct punctuation choice.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The park features hiking trails, a botanical garden[___] and a small amphitheater for outdoor performances.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Series of three items: 'hiking trails, a botanical garden, and a small amphitheater.' Standard comma before 'and' in a series (Oxford comma). C (,) is correct. A semicolon would only be needed if the items had internal commas.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The proposal was rejected[___] the board felt it lacked sufficient financial justification.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: "Because" makes the second clause dependent: "rejected because the board felt..." C is natural and correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The architect designed the museum[___] but the city lacked funding to build it for another decade.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two independent clauses joined by 'but' (FANBOYS) require a comma before 'but.' C (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Dr. Chen, the lead researcher on the project[___] presented her findings at the international conference.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The lead researcher on the project' is a NONRESTRICTIVE appositive (renames Dr. Chen). It needs commas on both sides. The opening comma is present; a closing comma is needed. C (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Although the weather forecast predicted rain[___] the outdoor ceremony proceeded as planned.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Although the weather forecast predicted rain' is an introductory dependent clause. Must be followed by a comma before the main clause. C (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The legislation was praised by economists[___] criticized by labor unions, and debated extensively in the press.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: This is a series: 'praised by economists, criticized by labor unions, and debated...' The comma after 'economists' is needed to separate the first and second items in the series. B (,) is correct.

grammar.title: Verb tense in context
grammar.lead: Real texts mix tenses constantly. These items give you a sentence with surrounding context — your job is to keep the timeline consistent.

leadTr.uz: Haqiqiy matnlarda zamonlar doim aralashadi. Bu mashqlarda kontekstli gap beriladi — vazifangiz voqealar chizig'ini izchil saqlash.
leadTr.ru: В настоящих текстах времена постоянно смешиваются. Здесь дано предложение с контекстом — ваша задача сохранить хронологию последовательной.

quiz.q:
Text: 'In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that mold [___] the bacteria in his petri dish, leading to the discovery of penicillin.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: The passage describes events in 1928 (past). 'Was killing' = past progressive, showing the ongoing action at the time of his observation. D is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'By the time the rescue team reached the stranded climbers, temperatures [___] below freezing for over eighteen hours.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'By the time [past event]' requires PAST PERFECT to show the temperature drop preceded the rescue. B (had dropped) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee recommended that the new facilities [___] accessible to all students with disabilities.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Recommended that' + SUBJECT + BASE VERB (subjunctive). C (be) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'If the treatment [___] more affordable, many patients who currently cannot access it would benefit significantly.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Contrary-to-fact condition (treatment is NOT currently affordable). 'Were' for all subjects in hypothetical conditions. C is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Researchers studying the fossilized remains [___] that the species went extinct approximately 65 million years ago.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Present perfect (have concluded) shows ongoing/current relevance — researchers have concluded (and this is the current scientific understanding). A is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'If the proposal [___] submitted before the deadline, it would have been considered for funding.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Contrary-to-fact past (it was NOT submitted): 'If it HAD BEEN submitted' + 'would have been considered.' C (had been) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The policy required that every employee [___] a mandatory safety training course before beginning work.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Required that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (complete) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'By 2030, the company [___] all of its operations to renewable energy sources.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'By 2030' (a future deadline) + FUTURE PERFECT to show completion by that point. C (will have converted) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'When the archaeologists [___] the site, they found evidence of a civilization far older than previously thought.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Sequential past events: 'excavated...found.' Both in simple past since they happened at roughly the same time (the finding was part of the excavation). D is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The judge insisted that the witness [___] the entire transcript without interruption.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Insisted that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. B (read) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Scientists [___] that the average global temperature has risen by approximately 1.1°C since pre-industrial times.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Current scientific consensus with past-to-present relevance → PRESENT PERFECT. C (have estimated) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'If renewable energy [___] cheaper faster, the transition from fossil fuels would have occurred decades earlier.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Contrary-to-fact past: 'If it HAD BECOME cheaper' + 'would have occurred.' B is correct.

grammar.title: Transitions between ideas
grammar.lead: However, therefore, meanwhile, in contrast… The right connector shows the logical relationship between two sentences. Read both sides of the blank before choosing.

leadTr.uz: However, therefore, meanwhile… To'g'ri bog'lovchi ikki gap orasidagi mantiqiy aloqani ko'rsatadi. Tanlashdan oldin bo'sh joyning ikkala tomonini ham o'qing.
leadTr.ru: However, therefore, meanwhile… Правильная связка показывает логическую связь между предложениями. Прочитайте обе стороны пропуска, прежде чем выбирать.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Early research on the drug showed promising results in laboratory settings. _____, clinical trials involving human subjects revealed serious side effects that had not appeared in animal models.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (promising results) CONTRASTS with S2 (serious side effects). This is a CONTRAST relationship → However.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The archaeologist found pottery suggesting settlement dating to 3000 BCE. _____, carbon dating of charcoal found in the same stratum confirmed the site was occupied during the early Bronze Age.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (pottery suggests early date) and S2 (carbon dating confirms similar date) are pointing in the SAME direction — S2 adds confirming evidence. ADDITION → Moreover.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Researchers have documented that people sleeping fewer than six hours show impaired reaction times and reduced working memory. _____, the prevalence of chronic sleep deprivation in industrialized nations continues to rise.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (documented harms) vs. S2 (deprivation is RISING despite this knowledge). Something continues DESPITE evidence against it. CONTRAST-DESPITE → Nevertheless.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The new manufacturing technique reduced production costs by 40%. _____, the savings were passed on to consumers in the form of lower retail prices.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Lower costs (cause) → lower prices for consumers (effect). CAUSE/EFFECT → Consequently.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Some historians argue the decline of Rome was primarily due to internal political corruption. _____, other scholars emphasize the role of external pressures, including migrations and military defeats along the empire's borders.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (internal factors) is contrasted with S2 (external factors — 'other scholars emphasize DIFFERENT causes'). CONTRAST → By contrast.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The new public transit system reduced average commute times significantly. _____, it lowered carbon emissions by reducing the number of private vehicles on major roadways.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (reduced commutes) and S2 (also reduced emissions) — the second ADDS another benefit of the same system. ADDITION → Additionally.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The medication showed no improvement over placebo in the controlled study. _____, subsequent real-world data collected from thousands of patients suggested meaningful benefits in the general population.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (no improvement over placebo) vs. S2 (real-world data shows benefits). Something positive happens DESPITE the controlled study finding. CONTRAST-DESPITE → Nevertheless.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The company invested heavily in employee training programs. _____, staff turnover rates fell sharply over the following three years, saving considerable recruitment and onboarding costs.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Investment in training (cause) → lower turnover (direct effect). CAUSE/EFFECT → As a result.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The prime minister had campaigned on a platform of fiscal restraint. _____, the budget she presented in her first year in office included the largest spending increase in a decade.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: The PM campaigned on restraint (expectation) but her budget was the opposite (largest spending increase). Clear reversal. CONTRAST → Yet.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Several studies have found that people make better decisions under moderate rather than extreme time pressure. _____, some amount of deadline stress appears to focus attention productively.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S2 explains/clarifies the MECHANISM behind S1's finding. 'That is' introduces a reformulation or explanation in other words. 'Therefore' would be wrong if S2 is a result but here it elaborates why.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The city's public library system has faced severe budget cuts over the past decade. _____, many branches have reduced their hours and eliminated programs for children and seniors.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Budget cuts (cause) → reduced hours and eliminated programs (effect). CAUSE/EFFECT → As a result.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Proponents of nuclear energy argue it produces reliable, low-carbon electricity at scale. _____, critics point to unresolved questions about waste storage and the safety of aging reactor infrastructure.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Proponents' view (positive) vs. critics' view (concerns). Two opposing perspectives. CONTRAST → However.
